questions.q: In a process, 701 J of heat is absorbed by a system and 394 J of work is done by the system. What is the change in internal energy (in J) for the process?
questions.solution:
Given, q = + 701 J (heat is absorbed, heance q is positive.)

W = - 394 J (work is done by the system, hence W is negative.)

By first law of thermodynamics;

Internal energy change, $\Delta \text{U} = \text{q} + \text{w}$
= + 701 J + (-394 J ) = + 307 J.

Hence, internal energy of the system increases by 307 J.

$T ∝ \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{V}}$

The value of $\gamma$ , i.e., $\left(\dfrac{{C}_{P}}{{C}_{V}}\right)$ of the gas will be

$T ∝ \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{V}}$

$TV^{\dfrac{1}{2}} =$ constant

So $\gamma - 1 = \dfrac{1}{2}$

questions.solution:
Bomb calorimeter is commonly used to find the heat of combustion of organic substances which consists of a sealed combustion chamber, called a bomb. If a process is run in a sealed container then no expansion or compression is allowed, so $w = 0$ and $\Delta U = q = - ve$ (exothermic reaction).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Diamonds are formed from graphite under high pressure in coal mines. Calculate the equilibrium pressure (in atm) at which graphite is converted to diamonds at 25<sup>o</sup>C (assumed constant) given densities of ${ρ}_{\text{graphite}} = 2 \text{g} / \text{cc} \text{ and } {ρ}_{\text{diamond}} = 3 \text{g} / \text{cc}  \left(\Delta {\text{G}}_{\text{f}}^{\text{o}}\right)$ for diamonds is 3 kJ m<sup>- 1</sup> from graphite
questions.solution:
Differential equation of free energy dG = VdP - SdT at constant temp. with change in allotropic modification there is a change in molar volume $∴$ $\text{d} \left(Δ \text{G}\right) = \left(Δ \text{V}\right) \text{dP}$.

$Δ \text{V} = \dfrac{{\text{M}}_{\text{Diamond}}}{{ρ}_{\text{Diamond}}} - \dfrac{{\text{M}}_{\text{graphite}}}{{ρ}_{\text{graphite}}} = \dfrac{1 2}{3} - \dfrac{1 2}{2}$

$Δ \text{V} = - 2 {\text{cm}}^{3} / \text{mole} = - 2 × 1 {0}^{- 6} {\text{m}}^{3} {\text{mole}}^{-1}$

$\mathop{∫ \text{d} \left(Δ \text{G}\right)}_{Δ {\text{G}}_{\text{f}}^{\text{o}} \text{at} 2 9 8 \text{K, 1 atm}}^{Δ {\text{G}}_{\text{f}}^{\text{o}} \text{at} 2 9 8 \text{K, p atm} = 0} = - 2 × 1 {0}^{- 6} {\text{m}}^{3} {\text{mole}}^{- 1} \mathop{∫ \text{dP}}_{\text{P} = \text{1 atm}}^{\text{P} = \text{p atm}}$

Because at equilibrium when diamonds are formed both the phases are in equilibrium $Δ {\text{G}}_{\text{f} \left(\text{Diamonds}\right)}^{\text{o}} \text{at} 2 9 8 \text{K ,} \text{P atm} = 0$

$\mathop{\overset{0}{∫} \text{d} \left(Δ \text{G}\right)}_{3 0 0 0 {\text{J mole}}^{-1}} = - 2 × 1 {0}^{- 6} {\text{m}}^{3} {\text{mole}}^{- 1} × 1 {0}^{5} {\text{Nm}}^{- 2} \mathop{∫ \text{dP}}_{\text{P} = \text{1 atm}}^{\text{P} = \text{p atm}}$

( 1 atm = 105 Nm- 2 )

0 - 3000 Joules mole- 1 = - 2 x 10- 1 J mole- 1 (P - 1)

$\dfrac{3 0 0 0}{0 \text{.} 2} = 1 5 0 0 0 = \left(\text{P} - 1\right)$

$∴$ P = 15001 atm.
